_provenance.purpose: Proves that granting the operator ADVERTISE on a seed page clears subcode 1713140. Nothing in the database could answer this: there is zero overlap between pages the BM tool has granted (bm_page_access_events action='granted') and pages used as audience seeds (meta_custom_audiences.source_meta.pageIds), so the remediation feature had to be tested live before being built.

setup.page_home_business: 527693220707294 (The Columbo Group) — the page is a CLIENT page there, is_owned_by_bm = false
setup.ad_account_business: 1927009767586803 (Electric Brixton) — deliberately a DIFFERENT business from the page's, since the control run already showed cross-business seeds create fine
setup.business_scoped_user_id: 122102828505388478 ("Matas Off/Pixel", ADMIN) — resolved by EMAIL, not name: /me reports "Matas Liebus" while the business-scoped identity is named "Matas Off/Pixel"

_provenance.reversibility: The grant was revoked immediately after the retry and the created audience deleted, restoring the prior state. Verified afterwards that no ZZ_PRC* audience remains on the ad account.

steps.action: POST /act_1073273492854557/customaudiences (page_followers_fb rule on the seed page)

error.message: (#2654) No permission for event source: Audience creation permission is missing for one or more event sources (ID: 260956420427418).

steps.conclusion: ADVERTISE alone is sufficient. FULL_CONTROL is NOT required.

steps.note: State restored; the created audience was deleted in the same run.

control_run.action: identical POST, same token, same ad account
control_run.conclusion: Same token succeeds on one page and fails on another, so the cause is per-page authorisation and NOT a missing token scope.
